synopsis: Brazil uses national workplace and mining regulation rather than a continent-wide South American machinery regime; NR-22 and NR-12 provide general mining, machinery, brake and operating requirements [f2285, f2130, f2288, f15579]. NR-22 covers occupational safety and health in mining and was last modified by Portaria MTE 105 on 29 January 2026, while NR-12 addresses machinery safety [f2286, f2287, f15578, f2796]. The reviewed Brazilian NR-22 and NR-12 text yielded no automatic-braking mandate, specifically no ISO 21815-style mandate prescribing target or speed tests [f2799, f2289, f15580]. These regulatory gaps mean “not found,” not “not required,” so the booklet does not establish an exemption from numeric acceptance requirements [f2297, f15586]. It also found no dedicated Brazilian off-road rule requiring an ML-based collision-avoidance function to meet a specified ML validation standard by 2028 [f2393].
